items.new: Such was the thunder of his voice that, despite their amazement, the men sprang over the rail. The pulleys whirled round in the blocks. With a lurch, the three boats dropped into the sea. And with a deft, offhand daring unknown in any other profession, the sailors leaped like goats down the rolling ship's side into the tossing boats below.

items.new: "Pull, pull, my good boys," said Starbuck, in the lowest possible but most intensely concentrated whisper to his men. The sharp fixed glance from his eyes, aimed straight ahead of the bow, seemed almost like two visible needles in two unerring binnacle compasses. He did not say much to his crew, nor did they say anything to him. Only the silence of the boat was at intervals piercingly broken by one of his peculiar whispers — now harsh with command, now soft with pleading.

items.new: A short rushing sound leaped out of the boat — it was the darted iron of Queequeg. Then all in one welded commotion came an invisible push from behind, while forward the boat seemed to strike a ledge. The sail collapsed and exploded. A gush of scalding vapor shot up nearby. Something rolled and tumbled like an earthquake beneath us. The whole crew was half-suffocated as they were tossed helter-skelter into the white curdling cream of the squall. Squall, whale, and harpoon had all blended together. And the whale, merely grazed by the iron, escaped.

items.new: Nor, given the ancient superstition of their race and the supernatural aura that seemed in many ways to surround the Pequod, were there lacking some seamen who swore that whenever and wherever it was sighted — at however remote times, or in however far-apart latitudes and longitudes — that unnearable spout was cast by one and the same whale, and that whale was Moby Dick. For a time, there also reigned a sense of peculiar dread at this flitting apparition, as if it were treacherously beckoning us on and on so that the monster might turn around upon us and tear us apart at last in the remotest and most savage seas.

items.new: But at last, when we turned eastward, the Cape winds began howling around us, and we rose and fell upon the long, troubled seas that lie there. When the ivory-tusked Pequod bowed sharply to the blast and gored the dark waves in her fury, until showers of silver chips — the foam-flakes — flew over her bulwarks, then all this desolate emptiness of life went away, but gave place to sights more dismal than before.

items.new: Southeastward from the Cape, off the distant Crozetts — a good cruising ground for Right Whalemen — a sail appeared ahead: the Goney, or Albatross by name. As she slowly drew near, from my lofty perch at the foremast-head I had a good view of that sight so remarkable to a newcomer in the far ocean fisheries: a whaler at sea, long absent from home.
